title: Identity normalization of scalar insertion
statement: Let J be an essentially small site, R→B a morphism of commutative ring sheaves, nY normalized scalar extensions, and g0 an identity geometry with ring and underlying inverse-image unitors rho0 and theta0. For any normalized scalar insertion i0 and any IdentityData d [def-weil-pbc-common-quotient-pullback-data], for every M in D(J,B), d.source.derived.inv(M) followed by i0.derived(M) followed by d.target.derived.hom(M) is the identity of the twice restricted M. No coefficient-flatness or quotient hypotheses are required.

source.place: Tags 06YY (derived base change), 0G7E (K-flat pullback), 0D6D (composition); sites-modules.tex Tags 03D7, 03EK, 03EL.

proof.text: The insertion section formula and the specified ordinary target unitor give insertion followed by target unitor equal to source unitor on every section, hence as module morphisms.

Apply the ordinary equality termwise on a flat-term K-flat complex. Paste the insertion representative square with the two unitor ModelIso squares. The common computation is the composite of two exact restriction computations, so is invertible; cancel it.

Restriction of homotopy localization to flat-term K-flat objects is a localization, as proved in RingedCoefficientPullbackComparison. Full faithfulness detects equality of the natural transformations on the derived category. Cancel the source unitor against its inverse.
